title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page: S is a connected scheme over Q, A is an abelian group (here apparently A = Z, with ξ(1) = −1/2), and ξ : A → Γ(S, G_m) is a homomorphism, equivalently a morphism of group schemes A_S → G_{m,S}. Pulling back the Kummer sequences 1 → μ_n → G_m → G_m → 1 along ξ gives a tower of étale extensions 1 → μ_n → E_n(ξ) → A_S → 1. Passing to the projective limit gives 1 → T_∞(G_m) → E_∞(ξ) → A_S → 1. A geometric point s̄ then gives a monodromy homomorphism π_1(S, s̄) → Aut(E_∞(ξ)_{s̄}) (341).

This page:
1. The fibre E_∞(ξ)_{s̄} is an extension 1 → T = T_∞(k̄*) ≅ Ẑ(1) → E → A → 1 (342), with T free of rank 1 over Ẑ.
2. The action (341) respects this extension structure. π_1 acts trivially on A, because A_S is constant. It acts on T through the cyclotomic character π_1(S) → π_1(Spec Q) → Ẑ* (343).
3. Let G be the group of automorphisms of E that preserve the extension, induce id_A, and act on T by a homothety μ_u ∈ Ẑ*. The map u ↦ μ_u is a canonical homomorphism G → Ẑ*.
4. Its kernel consists of the automorphisms u = id + φ∘p with φ ∈ Hom_Z(A, T). This gives the exact sequence 1 → Hom_Z(A, T_∞(k̄*)) → G → Ẑ* (345).

On the next page Grothendieck identifies the image of G → Ẑ* as the μ that fix the class of (342) in Ext(A, T). He lifts the cyclotomic character to χ_ξ : π_1 → G and notes that the image is open when S is of finite type over Q.

In modern terms this is the Kummer representation attached to ξ. For A = Z it is the map G_Q → Ẑ(1) ⋊ Ẑ* (the affine group), a ↦ (κ_a, χ), where κ_a is the Kummer cocycle of a = −1/2. It is the 'Kummer torsor' or affine-group packaging of Kummer theory. Such cocycles are exactly what enter the Galois action on the fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞} (abelianized/metabelian level, tangential base points). This is the purpose within La Longue Marche.
errors: No mathematical error. The transcription's '\pi_1(Q,\bar s)' means π_1(Spec Q, s̄) = Gal(Q̄/Q), so S is implicitly assumed to lie over Q.

When A is free (e.g. A = Z), the extension (342) is split as an abstract group extension, since Ext^1(Z, T) = 0. The class condition for the image of G → Ẑ* only becomes non-trivial when A has torsion. So for A = Z, G = T ⋊ Ẑ* and G → Ẑ* is surjective, consistent with the next page.

ideas.what: Kummer tower pulled back along ξ: A_S → G_m, giving the profinite extension E_∞(ξ) of A_S by Ẑ(1)
ideas.modern_name: Kummer torsor / Kummer extension attached to units; Kummer cocycle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical Kummer theory; this formulation is standard in Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points') and Ihara
ideas.where_published: Kummer theory in étale form appears in SGA 4/SGA 4½; this exact packaging is not known in published Grothendieck texts

ideas.what: Galois action on the fibre through the group G of extension automorphisms, with exact sequence 1 → Hom(A, Ẑ(1)) → G → Ẑ*
ideas.modern_name: Affine group Ẑ(1) ⋊ Ẑ*; Kummer–cyclotomic representation (metabelian quotient of the Galois action on π_1 of P^1 minus points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; Ihara, Deligne, Anderson–Ihara in the GT/π_1 context

ideas.what: Openness of the image of the cyclotomic character for S of finite type over Q (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Irreducibility of cyclotomic polynomials / open image of the cyclotomic character

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but entirely standard setup of Kummer theory as an extension with Galois action by the affine group Ẑ(1) ⋊ Ẑ*. It is preparatory material for the Galois action on fundamental groups in La Longue Marche, and contains nothing beyond well-known material.
transcription_corrections: The first line's uncertain word after 'structure d'extension' ('isotrope [?]') is more likely 'évidente'.

In (344) the inserted marginal text reads roughly 'on trouve un homom canonique' (with the crossed-out 'ce groupe ne dépend que de A'). The fragment 'u ↦ ce [?]' presumably means u ↦ μ (the homothety factor).
'{+0-+}connexe' on the previous page should simply be 'connexe'.
